text: How Memryoshka works with a vision-language model.
Each incoming frame goes through the model's own vision encoder, which turns it into about two hundred and fifty visual tokens.
The encoder's attention marks the tokens that matter most, and a small CLIP model gives each frame one search tag.
Each token is projected onto five hundred and twelve fixed directions, quantized, and written as a nested bit stream.
The memory has a fixed size. When it fills up, one price per bit shortens codes and drops the least useful tokens and frames.
When a question arrives, it is matched against the search tags, and the best-matching frames are decoded from their codes.
The decoded tokens go back to their places, with timestamps, and the frozen language model reads them with the question.
Nothing is trained. The vision encoder, the language model and the search model all stay frozen.
